chunks: All that is in the heavens and the earth sings the praises of God, the King, the Holy, Omnipotent, the Wise.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when the heavens and earth glorify God?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of 'Tasbih al-Kull' (the universal glorification of all beings), illustrating that every entity, whether conscious or not, actively proclaims God's perfection. The attributes of Al-Malik (The King) and Al-Quddus (The Holy) underscore His absolute sovereignty and purity from any defect, serving as a theological foundation for the Friday prayer's emphasis on communal submission and divine majesty.
